summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas and kidney transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and chronic heart failure was admitted for acute anemia and hypotension. She presented with a rapid drop in hematocrit from 24 to 19, lightheadedness, and chronic symptoms including daily nosebleeds, hand rash, and nail changes. She received three units of packed red blood cells, and her pancytopenia was attributed to immunosuppressive therapy with mycophenolate mofetil (CellCept), which was discontinued. An esophageal ulcer was found on EGD and treated with increased omeprazole, while colonoscopy revealed ischemic colitis likely due to recurrent hypotension. Dermatology evaluated her painful hand rash and thickened nails, initiated urea cream, and performed a biopsy pending further evaluation. Her warfarin was held due to epistaxis and restarted at discharge after 24 hours without bleeding. Levothyroxine was increased for elevated TSH. She stabilized hemodynamically, remained euvolemic, and was discharged to extended care with plans for outpatient follow-up in hematology, gastroenterology, and dermatology to monitor pending test results and medication management.
